ledger.note: 1960: Cyprus becomes independent from Britain on 16 August. "Cyprus officially attained independence on 16 August 1960" (infobox "Independence proclaimed: 16 August 1960"; London-Zurich Agreements 19 February 1959); "The UK retained the two Sovereign Base Areas of Akrotiri and Dhekelia".

region.text: the northern part of Cyprus: "Turkey occupies 36.2% of Cyprus"

ledger.note: 1974: the Turkish army lands at Kyrenia on 20 July, five days after the Greek junta's coup against Makarios (15 July). "Turkish forces landed in Cyprus on 20 July and captured 3% of the island before a ceasefire was declared"; "By the time the UN Security Council was able to obtain a ceasefire on 22 July ... a narrow path between Kyrenia and Nicosia". The region is the whole north, where the second phase took ground. [Reviewer eu-22-c, 2026-11-01: confidence 2, the page names only the Kyrenia-Nicosia corridor (3 % of the island) for July; the whole north is the researcher's zone.]

region.text: the northern part of Cyprus: "Turkey occupies 36.2% of Cyprus"

ledger.note: 1974: fighting ends in August with Turkey holding the north. Second phase launched 14 August ("On 14 August Turkey launched its ..." second offensive), "United Nations Security Council Resolution 360 adopted on 16 August 1974"; infobox "20 July - 18 August 1974", "Turkish victory". The Karpas, Morphou and Famagusta details are not on the page.

region.text: the northern part of Cyprus: "Turkey occupies 36.2% of Cyprus"

ledger.note: 1974: Turkey holds the northern 36 % of the island. Infobox: "Turkey occupies 36.2% of Cyprus"; "which eventually resulted in the Turkish occupation of 37% of Cyprus"; about 200,000 Greek Cypriots "fled their homes and became refugees in the south". The ceasefire line of August 1974 became the United Nations Buffer Zone. Turkey declared a "Federated Turkish State" on 13 February 1975 and the TRNC followed in 1983; the Republic never recognised either, so the land stays its own, occupied.

wars.name: Turkish invasion of Cyprus

zones.text: the northern part of Cyprus: "Turkey occupies 36.2% of Cyprus"

wars.outcome: Turkish victory (infobox, 20 July - 18 August 1974): Turkey captured 3 % of the island by the first ceasefire of 22 July and "approximately 36%" after the second offensive of 14 August; the Greek and Cypriot juntas collapsed on 23 and 24 July. The ceasefire line became the UN Buffer Zone.
wars.note: The coup that began it (15 July 1974) was carried out by sections of the Cypriot National Guard led by Greek officers; the Cyprus article names the Greek junta under Dimitrios Ioannides. The article gives two figures for the occupied share: 36.2 % in the infobox, 37 % in the text.

certainty.note: The coast is the frontier; the two Sovereign Base Areas are surveyed enclaves of the 1960 treaties.
The southern limit of the Turkish-held north is the 1974 ceasefire line, now the UN Buffer Zone (a line, not an agreed frontier). The sea limits are not drawn.

notes: Two pages (budget 1-2). Shared Wikidata: Cliopatria's "Cyprus Condominium" (cyprus-condominium, 688-965, Umayyad-Byzantine condominium, shape 11,438 km2 = the same whole-island outline) shares Q229 with this row because Q229 is the island; they are different states 1,000 years apart: two dossiers, not one. The Cliopatria Wikipedia title is "Cyprus". Cliopatria's row starts in 1961 though independence was on 16 August 1960: a 1960 keyframe is added. The Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (turkish-republic-of-northern-cyprus, Cliopatria 1976-2024, another part of eu-22) is the occupier's client; the republic of Turkey dossier already records contest_start 1974-07, contest_end and occupation_start 1974-08 against republic-of-cyprus and a vassal_start 1975-02 for the TFSC; this dossier mirrors the first three. Not drawn: the Turkish Cypriot enclaves of 1963-1974 (no boundaries on the pages), the 1983 declaration (month not given: "In 1983"), EU accession on 1 May 2004 (association, not territory), the Annan plan of 2004 (date not on the page). The British Sovereign Base Areas are British Overseas Territory (the british-overseas-territories row, 2000-2024); the minus term in each correction removes only one grid cell (the 12 km discs mirror the united-kingdom dossier). No ruler strip: the Cyprus page is silent on Makarios's dates and on most presidents.
